key_insight: Block-triangular joint drifting turns standard one-step trajectory data into a generative surrogate that can sample the next state directly in a single model evaluation per timestep.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast stochastic simulation for scientific computing workflows by reducing generative overhead while preserving accurate marginal and trajectory-level behavior.
method: Apply a projected drift field to the joint distribution of consecutive states, rather than only to the conditional next-state distribution.
Use a block-triangular architecture so the current-state marginal is preserved and the second block samples the conditional next-state distribution.
Generate stochastic trajectories without auxiliary diffusion, flow, or distillation steps between time steps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing accurate marginal and trajectory-dependent statistics and favorable accuracy-cost tradeoffs against deterministic, diffusion-, flow-, and distillation-based surrogates.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the joint-state drift projection is learned from limited trajectory data, especially when the conditional dynamics are highly multimodal or sparse.
paper_title: One-Step Generative Surrogate Models via Block-Triangular Joint Drifting
